newsitem.title: USA: Conn. lawmakers pass welfare, ethics bills - report.
newsitem.headline: Conn. lawmakers pass welfare, ethics bills - report.

text.p: Connecticut lawmakers passed bills on welfare, ethics and campaign finance during a special legislative session, the Hartford Courant reported Tuesday.
All three bills now go to Gov. John Rowland (R), who is expected to sign them.
The measures provide limited campaign finance reform, tighten restrictions on how much lawmakers can receive in gifts, food and drink, and modify the state's welfare system.
The welfare bill ends the state's general assistance program for individuals and establishes a broad safety net to help families get off welfare.
The bill proposes a $22 million program to help welfare recipients who have failed in a good-faith effort to find and keep a job and are approaching the state's new, 21-month limit on benefits.
The compromise welfare bill establishes a variety of state programs using the $300 million in federal block grant money the state expects to receive this year.
